rules.title: Double address-of
rules.statement: `&&v` (lexed as a single AND token) is the double address-of of `v`: it lowers to `&(&v)` with type `& & typeof(v)`. If `typeof(v)` is an error type the whole expression is an error.

rules.title: Address-of a module static is the global's stable address
rules.statement: `&S` where S is an unshadowed module static of non-array type yields the global's own address (a `'static` reference), preserving address identity; the reference is `&mut` iff S is a `mut` static. (No fresh stack copy is materialized.)

rules.title: &array → slice
rules.statement: `&a` where `a: [T; N]` yields a slice value `&[T]` with len = N (an unsized coercion at the point of borrow), not `&[T; N]`. This applies to array variables, array statics, and bare array literals `&[e0, .., e_{N-1}]`.

rules.title: &Box<[T]> deref-coerces to &[T]
rules.statement: `&b` where `b` is an owning slice (`Box<[T]>`) yields a borrowed `&[T]` view over the same {data,len} storage with no copy or move; mutability is inherited from the owning slice.

rules.title: &Box<Foo> deref-coerces to &Foo
rules.statement: `&b` where `b` is an owning DST reference (`Box<Foo>`) yields a borrowed `&Foo` with the same reference value re-typed non-owning; mutability is inherited.

rules.title: &*ptr reborrow
rules.statement: `&*p` where `p` has pointer kind (raw `*T`, `&T`, or `&mut T`) is a reborrow yielding `&(pointee(p))` preserving the reborrow shape; for a struct with a Deref impl `&*x` is `&(x.deref())`.

rules.title: &f[i] over user Index is a place reference
rules.statement: `&f[i]` over a value implementing the Index trait yields the place reference returned by `index()` directly (no intermediate deref or temporary).

rules.title: &a[range] is the slice value itself
rules.statement: `&e` where `e` is a range-index `a[i..j]` that already has slice kind `&[T]` yields that slice value unchanged (no additional reference wrapper), since the slice kind is already the borrowed fat form.

rules.title: &<rvalue> spills to a stack temporary
rules.statement: `&e` for a non-place expression `e` materializes `e` into a stack temporary and yields `&typeof(e)`. If `typeof(e)` is an error type the expression is an error.

rules.title: Negated integer literal folds the sign
rules.statement: `-L` where L is an integer literal is parsed as the single negative literal `-L`, so the minimum suffixed value (e.g. `-128i8`) is accepted even though the bare positive literal would be out of range for its type.

rules.title: Unary operators dispatch to Neg/Not impls on struct operands
rules.statement: For a struct operand, `-x` resolves to the `Neg::neg(self)->Self` method and `!x` to the `Not::not(self)->Self` method via mangled `<Type>__neg`/`<Type>__not` signature lookup; when found, the unary expression becomes that method call.

rules.title: Unary minus requires a numeric operand
rules.statement: `-x` on a non-struct operand requires `x` to be of numeric type (else a type error); the result type equals the operand type.

rules.title: Unary minus on an unsigned type is rejected
rules.statement: `-x` where `x` has any unsigned integer type (u8/u16/u24/u32/u56/u64/u128) is a compile error; an explicit cast to a signed type is required (e.g. `-(x as i64)`).
rules.divergence: Extra unsigned widths u24/u56 are Logos-only (A11); the unary-minus-on-unsigned rejection itself matches Rust (no `Neg` impl for unsigned).

rules.title: Unary ! is logical-not on bool and bitwise-not on integers
rules.statement: `!x` requires `x` to be `bool` (result `bool`) or an integer type (result = operand type; an untyped integer literal becomes `i32`); any other operand type is a type error.

rules.title: Dereference routes through a Deref impl
rules.statement: `*x` for any type implementing Deref (Box/Rc/Arc/user, including generic impls) lowers to `*(x.deref())` via the generic-aware method machinery.

rules.title: Dereference of a non-pointer value is identity
rules.statement: `*x` where `x` is neither a raw pointer nor a reference (and has no Deref impl) yields `x` unchanged rather than an error.
rules.divergence: Rust rejects `*x` on a non-pointer; Logos relaxes it to identity to accept faithful Rust loop imports (B3-bg-07), since `for i in &v` already yields T not &T.

rules.title: Raw pointer dereference requires unsafe
rules.statement: `*p` where `p` is a raw pointer `*T` is only permitted inside an unsafe context; otherwise it is an error. The result type is the pointee type.

rules.title: Package-qualified call constrains free-fn resolution to that package
rules.statement: A call `pkg.path::fn(args)` carries a dotted package qualifier (RECEIVER + QUAL_PARTS joined by `.`); free-function resolution for that call is restricted to the named package.
rules.divergence: A9: packages are `.`-separated, items reached via `::`.

rules.title: Qualified call with no matching free fn is a type-member call
rules.statement: If a qualified `pkg.path.Member(args)` has no free function of that name in the package, the last dotted segment is interpreted as a type and the call is resolved as a static/associated method call `pkg.path.Type::method(...)`. A matching free function takes precedence.

rules.title: Tuple-struct constructor call
rules.statement: `Foo(a0, .., a_{n-1})` where Foo is a tuple struct constructs a struct literal with positional fields named "0".."n-1"; argument count must equal the field count; for a generic tuple struct the struct type-args are inferred by unifying each argument type against the declared field type.

rules.title: Callee resolution to closure or fn-pointer
rules.statement: A call `x(args)` treats `x` as callable when its type is a Closure or fn-value kind; `Box<dyn Fn*>` (Box<Closure>) is unwrapped to its inner Closure, and an Fn-bounded generic type-param `F` is treated as a closure with the bound's `fn_params`/`fn_ret` signature.
rules.divergence: A10: dyn Fn* collapses to the bare Closure type.

rules.title: Call auto-derefs a reference to a callable
rules.statement: `x(args)` where `x: &fn(..)` / `&mut fn(..)` / `&F` (reference to a callable or Fn-bounded param) auto-dereferences the reference to load the inner fn-pointer/closure before calling.

rules.title: Closure/fn-ptr call arity and argument typing
rules.statement: A closure/fn-ptr call requires argument count to equal the callable's parameter count; each argument is coerced to its parameter type and must be type-compatible; the result type is the callable's return type, or `()` (void) if absent.

rules.title: By-value move-type arguments to a callable are moved
rules.statement: In a closure/fn-ptr call `f(args)`, a by-value concrete move-type argument transfers ownership into the callee (source marked moved). By-reference parameters and TypeVar-typed arguments are excluded.

rules.title: Dereferencing a move-typed Box moves the value out and frees the box
rules.statement: `*b` where `b` is a bare variable of type `Box<T>` and `T` is a move (non-Copy) type consumes `b`, moves the boxed value out, and frees the box without dropping the content (Rust's built-in `*b` move; desugars to `box_take::<T>(b)` with `T` inferred). This is the canonical `let s = *b` form. For a Copy element `T`, `*b` copies the value out and leaves `b` live (normal deref path); non-Box derefs also use the normal copy/deref path.
